description: A tooth bound in cord and hide, meant to be worn. The wrapping is careful; the tooth is not the wearer's.
lore: Nine turns of cord, a hide collar cut to sit flat against the crown, a bead of amber set dead centre so it faces outward when the thing hangs. That is an evening's work, and it was not an evening spent on oneself: whoever took this tooth wrapped it up and handed it over, which is the exact opposite of what a trophy is for.

After that it does the job all of them do. A stranger asks what it is. You tell them what it came off and where you were standing and who was standing with you, and they listen, because they asked first. [[characters/ef25b1f0|Bettany]] has thirty-odd of these written into [[lore/the_chronicle|the Chronicle]] and not one of the entries is really about a tooth. Thirty gold at a counter buys you the object without the evening, and the trade knows perfectly well which half was worth having, and sells the other one anyway.
gm_notes: A charm as a conversation starter is a charm as maintenance — it gets its own story told aloud a few times a year. Never state that in prose; the record demonstrates it and stops.
